_decoded_content.title: Support for adding and configuring all "plugins" in Meltano UI
_decoded_content.description:
Per https://gitlab.com/meltano/meltano/-/issues/3527#note_960415549

Without writing a ton of code, we should try to open up _all_ plugin types to being added and configured via Meltano UI.

- Option A: Consolidate `Extractors` and `Loaders` into `Plugins`.
- Option B: Add one more Page for `Utilities` or `Plugins` or `Other Plugins`.
- Option C: Add another page for each plugin type.

I think my personal preference is just to have a single "Plugins" page where plugins are added and configured (option A). But what we choose will depend on many factors including long-term product direction and relative effort of each approach after sizing/scoping.

_decoded_content.title: Meltano UI "Add extractor/loader" experience post-2.0
_decoded_content.description:
After #3283+ lands, we'll want to review the functionality of Meltano UI as it relates to adding plugins.

A few updates I can see being fairly important:

1. (Lower pri.) Allowing the user to define settings in the UI if they are not already set.
   - In the meanwhile, we could simply instruct the users to do this in the CLI.
2. (Higher pri.) Updating the UI so the user can add plugins from the hub, perhaps using the API endpoints or by using the output of `meltano discover`.
3. (Medium pri.) Allowing other plugins to be added/configured in the UI, in addition to extractors and loaders.

_decoded_content.title: Missing settings in the UI for _state / _catalog and settings in inherited plugins
_decoded_content.description:
### What is the current *bug* behavior?
When adding the `_state` or `_catalog` as as setting in a plugin, this setting is recongnized (value is taken into account), but the setting is not shown in the plugin configuration in the UI. Those two settings are extra settings for an extractor plugins. The [state](https://meltano.com/docs/plugins.html#state-extra) and the [catalog](https://meltano.com/docs/plugins.html#catalog-extra) are both documented.

Additionaly, settings in inherited plugins (non inherited settings) are not shown in the plugin configuration in the UI. But once configured over the CLI, the setting is visible in the UI.



### What is the expected *correct* behavior?
All the plugin relaated settings should be shown and editable in the UI (unless set as non editable). 



### Steps to reproduce
Set _state and _catalog as followed for an extractor plugin:
```
settings:
 - name: _state
   kind: string
 - name: _catalog
   kind: string
```

For the problem with inheritent settings you will see it by configurating a target as follows:
```
  - name: target-stitch
    namespace: target_stitch
    pip_url: target-stitch
    executable: target-stitch
    settings:
    - name: client_id
      kind: integer
    - name: small_batch_url
      kind: string
    - name: big_batch_url
      kind: string
  - name: target-stitch-test
    inherit_from: target-stitch
    settings:
      - name: token
        kind: password
```

The token won't be visible when configurating over the UI. But as soon as you set the token over the UI with the following command: 

`meltano config target-stitch-test set token test123`

You will now see the token field in the UI and be able to edit it.

_decoded_content.title: Change casing to sentence case for titles, headings, labels, menu items, and buttons
_decoded_content.description:
### Problem

Maybe the intention _is_ to use title case everywhere but it looks unnecessary.

### Proposal

Since this is already using some buttons from the [Pajamas Design System](https://design.gitlab.com/) why not also adopt some of the [punctuation guidelines](https://design.gitlab.com/content/punctuation), too?

> Use sentence case for titles, headings, labels, menu items, and buttons. Use title case when referring to features or products. Note that some features are also objects.

This means that button labels should change from _Account Settings_ to _Account settings_, Edit Selections to _Edit selections_, etc. In contrast, step marker details can remain as is (e.g. _Source Connectors_, _Source Selections_, etc.)

_decoded_content.title: Provide an intuitive way to manage anonymous usage data collection
_decoded_content.description:
### Background

Currently, [anonymous usage data](https://meltano.com/docs/environment-variables.html#anonymous-usage-data) collection is enabled by default for new projects unless explicitly disabled, for new, existing, or all projects, using the `--no_usage_stats` flag during project creation from the CLI, b) the `send_anonymous_usage_stats` setting in the `meltano.yml` file, or c) the `MELTANO_DISABLE_TRACKING` environment variable as described in the documentation.

### Problem

This makes it harder for someone to disable anonymous usage data for new, existing, or all projects which can have a negative impact on the product since usage data collection is closely related to privacy issues.

### Proposal

Let's make it easier to disable or enable anonymous usage data collection through the user interface.
1. This could include showing a toast message the first time you load the project mentioning usage data collection and provide an action button to disable usage data collection which is currently enabled by default.
2. In addition, providing a preference option in user profile settings could help make this more clear to the user.

### Benefits

Providing an option to disable usage data collection can have a positive impact on the product and new users since usage data collection is closely related to privacy issues.

### Design

TBD

### Risk

The current [focus](https://meltano.com/docs/roadmap.html#focus) of the team is to grow [Monthly Active UI Users (MAUI)](https://meltano.com/docs/roadmap.html#metrics) based on the anonymous usage data which is [enabled by default](https://meltano.com/docs/environment-variables.html#anonymous-usage-data).

_decoded_content.title: Use a single port for serving the web app
_decoded_content.description:
### Problem

It's common for the built-in server in [Flask](https://flask.palletsprojects.com/en/1.1.x/quickstart/#quickstart) to use port `5000`. It's also common to use port `8080` to serve a web app.

However, documentation, tutorials, CLI output, and more reference the web app running on port `5000` or `8080`. This can cause some confusion on which port to expect for accessing the web app. This gets even more confusing when the web app is served on both ports locally when running `meltano ui` and in some cases the app is not even fully working, see https://gitlab.com/meltano/meltano/issues/1291.

### Proposal

Let's remove this confusion by doing the following:
1. Always reference web app access through the `8080` port.
2. Remove the web app from being served on the `5000` port.

### Risk

This affects both app configuration and documentation.

_decoded_content.title: Add way in UI to add discoverable plugin that already exists another time using inheritance
_decoded_content.description:
Like http://meltano.com/docs/plugin-management.html#explicit-inheritance, but in the UI.

I imagine that discoverable plugins would _not_ disappear from the "Available" section on the Extractors or Loaders page, and that users would have an option to hit "Add to project" another time.
The user would need to enter a unique name for the new plugin (since the discoverable plugin's own name was already used the first time it was added to the project using a [shadowing definition](http://meltano.com/docs/project.html#shadowing-plugin-definitions)).
